- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment turns bullish sharply (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model often lags — anticipate 1–3 day delay in price reaction; adjust forecast to reflect momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecasts 30d price > 20% above recent 10d average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movement — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is positive or neutral in last 5 days.
